sequence_notes.rule: Every shot is built in layers: Veo animates the world with the camera locked, Premiere does every camera move, cut and grade, and ffmpeg draws every word (TRANSFERRING…, HEADCOUNT 0, the prompter) and the invader flips.
sequence_notes.why: Camera movement is what makes Veo redraw a scene, so locking it stops that. Premiere's API cannot write text. The exceptions are the abstract signal plates, which have no window grid, so Veo may rush the camera there like the cable clip.

sequence_notes.rule: The rooms can be match-cuts: half a second of the opening's own clip, then a hard cut on the beat to the same frame, empty.
sequence_notes.why: Every empty still was made by editing the original, so the frames should line up. A hard cut makes the viewer do the subtraction: they were here, now they're not. This is strongest on the trading floor, where they were laughing.
sequence_notes.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (hard cut); picks.md (Kai: 'they were laughing before and then they're not')

sequence_notes.rule: Signal plates are 1–1.5s cutaways, cut in amongst the bigger shots on the beat grid (0.345s at 174 BPM).
sequence_notes.why: Kai's note: 'five or six of these… to edit in amongst other scenes.' They're glue, not destinations.

sequence_notes.rule: Flashes 3 a second or fewer (the invader strobe, the six flips, the press array).
Generate 6s, use 1–3s. Count 1, Omni 1.1 Flash, Frames, 16:9.
sequence_notes.why: Long clips redraw the scene after a few seconds, so we only need the clean start.
